pairs.subject: browser-credential-boundary
pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/library/page.tsx:42 The Library reads its index only on the server, through the server-only port, and the client island gets Server Action references and same-origin media URLs, so the browser holds no credential for any dependency. A case-insensitive search of app/(studio)/library for NEXT_PUBLIC, apiKey/api_key, authorization, createClient, supabase, anon_key, signedUrl and x-api-key found no hits.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/library/page.tsx:41 The only env-derived value (SIDE, from unprefixed GRAVITONE_PRODUCE_SIDE in the server-only _port) is used in the Server Component. No browser-read config value exists in this context.

app/(studio)/library/_library/Library.tsx:86 The client calls a same-origin Server Action for the app's own index. No privileged upstream or vendor secret is reached from this screen, so nothing needs brokering.
app/(studio)/library/fixture-tone/route.ts:24 The context's one route builds a WAV in memory and makes no outbound fetch, so no destination arrives as data.

app/(studio)/library/page.tsx:44 The error message shown comes from the app's own local index, not from an upstream behind a broker, and the project deliberately renders real store errors verbatim. That exposes no third-party topology.
app/(studio)/library/page.tsx:43 Kind and facet counts are computed server-side by the port. No browser role queries a hosted store's tables or views directly.

app/(studio)/library/_library/DetailView.tsx:143 The client renders a shaped ShownDetail projection the server built. There is no schema a public role can read, so there is no regime-one column grant to judge.

app/(studio)/library/_library/Library.tsx:143 Writes go through a Server Action, so the server is the only client of the store. This matches the technique's 'your code is the only client' exclusion; there are no row policies to write.
app/(studio)/library/_library/Library.tsx:89 The only outcome surface is a toast of an action's error code. No debug or log stream renders requests that carried credentials.
